3090545.findings: Single-door cabinet of bedside size in a red-brown hardwood that looks like Tasmanian blackwood or myrtle (species not verified). Top is banded in three timbers (dark outer, pale centre, dark outer). Door has two flat panels split by a centre stile, a brass oval flush catch plate, brass butt hinges, square tapered legs and a shaped bracket under the front rail. Photo 2 shows an old paper maker's label on the rough, unfinished back or underside: printed COOGAN'S TASMANIA. with printed fields Job No., Order No., Design No., Bench No., Dept., Fxd. by. Handwritten entries read in part: Order No. 900 (probable), Design No. 17 (probable), Bench No. 104, Dept. 3 (probable). The Job No. and Fxd. by entries are illegible. The label is water stained and looks original to the weathered surface it sits on. Coogan's (W. Coogan and Co) was a large Tasmanian furniture maker with factories in Hobart and Burnie working in Tasmanian timbers (Examiner article https://www.examiner.com.au/story/6032721/designs-on-value-and-style/ , read 19/10/2026), so the label supports a Tasmanian factory-made piece rather than a one-off. A label alone does not prove the piece is untouched, and the glossy front finish may be a later refinish. 'Arts and Crafts' in the title fits the plain panelled door and tapered legs. Date not confirmed, probably early to mid 20th century. Size claim (H-76 L-61 D-44 cm) cannot be checked.
3090545.condition: Front, top and side look clean with a glossy finish, possibly refinished. No splits, chips or lifted veneer visible in the photos. Interior, shelf and back panel condition not shown. The back or underside is weathered and rough.
3090545.reason: Readable COOGAN'S TASMANIA maker's label on a clean Tasmanian-style timber cabinet; local-interest piece with modest but real resale value.
3090545.marks_read: Paper label: COOGAN'S TASMANIA. (printed); handwritten Order No. 900?, Design No. 17?, Bench No. 104, Dept. 3?; Job No. and Fxd. by illegible
